title: Block: Prefix Sum Plus a Hashmap
oneLiner: Find the longest subarray that sums to k by remembering where each running sum first appeared.
keyTakeaway: A subarray sums to k when two running sums differ by k. Seed the map with {0: -1} so subarrays starting at index 0 count, and keep only the first index of each sum.
explanation:
Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray of nums whose sum is exactly k, or 0 if there is none. Values can be negative, which is why a sliding window doesn't work here.

Walk the array keeping the running sum. If sum - k was seen before at index j, the elements after j up to here sum to k, so i - j is a candidate. Store each running sum's index only the first time you see it: the earliest start gives the longest subarray. Subarray Sum Equals K is this block with counts in the map instead of indices.

starterCode.python:
def longest_subarray_sum_k(nums, k):
    # 1. Make a map from running sum to the first index it appeared at, seeded with {0: -1} for the empty prefix.
    # 2. Walk the array keeping a running sum.
    # 3. If sum - k is in the map, the subarray after that index sums to k: update the best length.
    # 4. Store the sum's index only if the sum is not in the map yet.
    # 5. Return the best length.
    return 0

gotchas: Forgetting the {0: -1} seed, which misses subarrays that start at index 0.
Overwriting a sum's index with a later one, which shortens the subarrays found.

complexity.note: One pass with O(1) average map work; up to n distinct running sums are stored.
